Title: Trial by social media must cease
Article:
LETTERS:
Datuk Seri Mohd Shuhaily Mohd Zain  has been charged in court for causing hurt and proceedings have yet to commence. The evidence against him has yet to unfold but the comments on social media are raging.
This has to cease as it does not do any party, any favours in ensuring that justice will be done.
It is extremely perturbing this incident has to be ventilated in court as it involves essential enforcement agencies of the government and the possibility of revealing how covert operations, intelligence, evidence from observation, deployment, instructions, are carried out as it will to some extent, become public knowledge.
It does not augur well for the agencies concerned in particular to the image of all the relevant parties involved notwithstanding the effect it will have on similar duties in future.
Earlier when this incident went viral on social media, I was of the opinion that this would have been sorted out by the respective superiors of the parties concerned.
Now that the Attorney-General's Chambers has decided to bring charges against Suhaily, we must now allow the law to take it's course although there are concerns as to how, this proceeding being ventilated in open court, can affect the structure of command and control within these agencies notwithstanding the effect it may have in public trust and confidence.
Although the matter is a summons case and can be compounded, it carries far reaching implications in all the careers and personal impact in the respective parties background in their respective agencies.
The proportion of the alleged offence and the pursuit of it in open court, may not commensurate with the overall negative impact it can have.
It is also humbly opined that the law protects all enforcement personnel, when carrying out their duties in good faith, although they may still be subjected to disciplinary admonishment if they acted unethically and improperly out of standard operating procedures.
Discretion must always be the better part of valour.
G. SELVA
Ipoh
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 6 cases of illegal racing detected in KL operation
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Six cases of illegal racing and speed testing were detected during an overnight enforcement operation in Kuala Lumpur, with nine motorcycles seized
Kuala Lumpur Road Transport Department (RTD) director Hamidi Adam said the operation, conducted jointly with the department's Putrajaya headquarters, targeted illegal racing and dangerous riding along Jalan Raja Laut, Jalan Ampang and the city centre.
The operation involved 37 enforcement personnel and ran from "10pm yesterday to 5am today", he said in a statement.
Hamidi said 35 vehicles were inspected during the seven-hour operation, with enforcement action taken against 11.
A total of 47 notices were issued for various offences, including driving without a valid licence, expired driving licences and motor vehicle licences, lack of insurance coverage and technical violations.
Other offences included unauthorised vehicle modifications, non-compliant registration plates and exhaust systems.
"Nine motorcycles were also seized," he said.
Hamidi said Section 42A was a new provision under the Road Transport Act aimed at strengthening enforcement against illegal racing and speed testing.
Under Section 42A, first-time offenders face fines of between RM2,000 and RM10,000, imprisonment of up to two years, or both, upon conviction.
Repeat offenders face heavier penalties, including fines ranging from RM5,000 to RM20,000, imprisonment of up to five years, or both.
Hamidi said public roads were not racing circuits.
"The thrill sought by a handful of individuals should not come at the expense of the safety of other road users."

Title: Lim Guan Eng calls for open tender to develop local Waze alternative
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The government should hold an open tender to develop a local road navigation app as an alternative to Waze, following criticism of TuJu's performance.
DAP adviser Lim Guan Eng said the appointment of Prosignal Consortium Sdn Bhd, the private company behind TuJu, raised questions about the lack of an open tender and warranted an explanation.
He said the app had drawn public criticism, with questions also raised about its developer, ownership, links to former civil servants and how the project was awarded.
"The government should open a tender so that capable local companies, especially those owned by young people, have a fair opportunity to develop a better navigation app.
"I am confident that many young Malaysians have the talent to produce a better road navigation app if given the opportunity, sufficient funding and room to compete through an open tender," he said in a statement.
Lim said the government should allow sufficient time to develop and test any alternative navigation app, ensuring it was reliable before being introduced to users.
He also proposed using existing funding facilities to help developers produce a minimum viable product without giving up equity.
These include Cradle Fund's CIP SPARK programme, which offers conditional grants of up to RM150,000, and financing of up to RM600,000 for technology product commercialisation.
He also cited the Malaysia Digital Catalyst grant by the Malaysia Digital Economy Corporation, which offers up to RM1 million, and the Malaysia Digital Acceleration Grant, which provides up to RM2 million to support the development and expansion of digital solutions.
"In addition, the Cradle Elevate programme offers financing of between RM500,000 and RM2 million to support start-ups moving from early validation to the growth phase.
"These facilities can give local companies the opportunity to develop a navigation app that meets users' needs," he added.
Last week, the government encouraged the public to use TuJu, a local navigation app developed by the Malaysian Highway Authority, as an alternative to Waze.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the move followed concerns over
security risks
involving users' personal information and movement data when using Waze, which he said was subject to Israeli government laws.
Last Friday, Anwar apologised to members of the public who had encountered
problems
using TuJu, following feedback that the app had shortcomings and needed improvement.

Title: Police to question content creator who entered Zalina Azman's house
Article:
SHAH ALAM: Police will call in a content creator who entered the home of former television personality Zalina Azman here and shared footage of the property on social media for an explanation.
Shah Alam district police chief Assistant Commissioner Sarudin Samah said the individual would be called in to explain his actions.
"However, police will first review the matter to determine what action can be taken," he told Harian Metro.
Sarudin said investigations into Zalina's disappearance were ongoing, but there were still no strong leads to warrant further action.
"Police have acted on every piece of information and new lead received.
"However, there are still no strong leads concerning the woman's disappearance," he said.
He said police had also checked Immigration Department records of entries and exits but had found no new developments in the case.
On claims that the house had been broken into, Sarudin said the condition of the property indicated that someone had entered it previously.
Police checks found that four air-conditioning units at the house had been broken, while a sink pipe was also reported missing, he said.
He added that Section 6 police station continued to conduct regular patrols in the residential area.
The case resurfaced after a content creator visited Zalina's home to inspect the property amid the mystery surrounding her disappearance in November 2021.
In his latest update, the content creator said an upstairs room that had been locked during his first visit was now open and accessible.
Several photographs he shared showed various items believed to belong to Zalina still inside the house, including Indonesian rupiah coins, bank books, clothing, toiletries and other personal belongings.
However, the house appeared to be in disarray, with several electrical appliances, including air-conditioning units, seemingly removed.
Zalina was reported missing after she could not be contacted from Nov 24, 2021, when her son, Mikhael Norman, tried to reach her to inform her that his father had been admitted to hospital.
Her disappearance remains a mystery, with police retaining her status as a missing person as there is no conclusive evidence that she has died or left the country.
The case remains open as police continue their investigations and review any new leads.

Title: Experts warn against blanket Waze ban without consultation
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The government should consult industry experts before deciding whether to ban Waze, as a blanket ban could create problems for users and drivers.
Cybersecurity expert Fong Choong Fook said the government could set up a committee or organise an open forum to gather feedback before deciding on the issue.
He said other applications, including WhatsApp and Instagram, also collected location information and personal data, raising similar concerns.
"If we are concerned about Waze collecting our data, we should also be concerned about WhatsApp, Instagram and many other applications, particularly those with Israeli connections," he told the New Straits Times.
Fong said the government should consider recommending suitable alternatives rather than imposing an immediate ban, adding that these must offer features comparable to Waze.
"I have tried the local alternative myself, and I find it less user-friendly than Waze. Of course, there are other alternatives, such as Apple Maps and Google Maps," said the LGMS Bhd chief executive officer.
Fong said applications could collect data beyond location information, including access to users' contact lists, cameras, microphones and photo galleries.
Meanwhile, Gabungan eHailing Malaysia (GEM) chief activist Jose Rizal said the authorities should consult industry stakeholders before making a nationwide decision that could affect gig workers' livelihoods.
He said any changes must not undermine drivers' earnings, passenger service quality or the stability of the e-hailing sector.
"Drivers can adapt, but platforms and policymakers must also take responsibility for ensuring a fair and orderly transition," he said.
Jose said the impact of a Waze ban would vary among drivers, as some already used other navigation applications.
On Saturday, Puchong member of parliament
Yeo Bee Yin
also called for consultation with industry experts and navigation technology specialists before any decision on a nationwide ban.
Yeo, who is also DAP national publicity secretary, said a hasty decision could disrupt millions of Malaysians who rely on Waze for their daily commutes, logistics and livelihoods.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has ordered
civil servants
to stop using Waze over concerns that sensitive government information could be compromised, while the public has been urged to follow suit.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Dewan Rakyat Speaker disappointed Takiyuddin made mediation proposal public before his response
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Dewan Rakyat Speaker Tan Sri Johari Abdul is disappointed with Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan's (PN-Kota Baru) decision to make his mediation proposal public without waiting for a response from him.
Johari said he had earlier given Takiyuddin until last Thursday to withdraw his remark involving the word "munafik", following a complaint by RSN Rayer (PH-Jelutong).
Johari said Takiyuddin then sent him a letter stating that he was unwilling to withdraw the remark and proposing mediation involving the Speaker, Rayer and himself.
He said the letter was received about 5pm that day, but he only read it the following day.
"I find it rather disappointing. When he wrote to me, he should have given me an opportunity to respond first, whether I agreed with his proposal or not.
"Instead, he made it public, putting me in a rather difficult position by pressuring me to respond," he said.
It was previously reported that Rayer
raised the issue after
Takiyuddin cited a hadith on the three traits of a hypocrite – lying when speaking, breaking promises and betraying trust – during the 2027 Budget debate.
Johari had asked Takiyuddin to
withdraw
the word, either in the House or through a letter to him.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Langkawi duty-free status not meant to help the rich avoid luxury car taxes
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The duty-free status of Langkawi is not intended to allow wealthy individuals to keep luxury vehicles on the island for several years before bringing them into the Principal Customs Area to avoid paying higher taxes.
Deputy Finance Minister Liew Chin Tong said changes to the duty and tax exemption policy for vehicles were introduced not only to address revenue leakage but also to discourage such business practices.
"At its core, this is a business model that we do not wish to promote, and we hope this policy will be accepted by all citizens," he said in reply to a supplementary question from Datuk Mohd Suhaimi Abdullah (PN-Langkawi) during the Special Chamber session in the Dewan Rakyat today.
Mohd Suhaimi had sought clarification on the government's review of the RM300,000 threshold for vehicle tax exemptions in Langkawi and called for stricter enforcement to prevent abuse of the facilities.
Liew acknowledged that some business operators would be affected by the policy but stressed that local residents would not be impacted.
Earlier, he said that, effective Jan 1, 2026, duty and tax exemptions for vehicles would be capped at a value of RM300,000 to prevent wealthy individuals from abusing the incentives to acquire luxury vehicles.
He said the threshold was reasonable and sufficient to meet the needs of local residents, car rental operators, taxi services and commercial vehicle users, while ensuring that the exemptions remained focused on vehicles used for daily activities and local business operations.
"Although there have been changes to the tax exemption policy for certain products on Langkawi Island, its status as a Duty-Free Island remains in effect," he added.
Meanwhile, Liew said the government had announced in Budget 2027 an increase in the eligibility threshold for duty-free purchases by visitors and tourists from RM1,000 to RM10,000.
He said the revised threshold covered several additional categories of goods, including fashion accessories such as watches and handbags, electrical and electronic items, and textiles, while excluding tobacco products and motor vehicles.
"Raising the value limit allows both domestic and international tourists to spend more, which in turn generates a direct economic spillover for duty-free shop owners and local entrepreneurs in Langkawi.
"At the same time, the requirement for a minimum 48-hour stay will boost the hospitality sector, homestays, transport services, and the food and beverage industry, ensuring that economic benefits are widely enjoyed across the island's entire tourism ecosystem," he said.
Liew added that the government was also updating and expanding the list of Langkawi-made goods eligible for import duty exemptions when brought into the Principal Customs Area, increasing the number of items from 23 to 29.
He said the measure would particularly benefit micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) in Langkawi.
Both measures will take effect on Jan 1, 2027, he added.

Title: Women must shape media narratives, says NST editor
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Women should have the power to shape how the world is portrayed, not merely appear in it, said New Straits Times Life & Times editor Intan Maizura Ahmad Kamal.
"Representation isn't simply about seeing more women in the picture; it's about giving women the power to help shape the picture," she said.
Intan was speaking on "Women, Media and the Power of Representation: Shaping Inclusive Cities" at a plenary forum on catalysts for peace,
dialogue and social cohesion
at the third Southeast Asia Dialogue Cities Conference.
Intan said such decisions were made in newsrooms every day, often through small choices about which stories and voices received space.
She said the 30 per cent target should ensure
women had enough
presence and influence to shape decisions, rather than simply meet a numerical goal.
"A newsroom decision can become a public perception, and a public perception can influence how communities see one another.
"That's power, and it's a responsibility which we should never take lightly," she said.
Intan said women were often introduced through their relationships, as someone's wife, mother or daughter, or as a caregiver, victim or survivor.
"These identities do matter, but they should never become the boundaries of a woman's identity," she said.
She outlined three questions she asks of every story: who gets to be seen, how they are being seen, and what happens after they are seen.
On inclusive cities, she said a city was more than its buildings and that the stories told about its people formed part of how it understood itself.
"If the media constantly presents difference as something threatening, we shouldn't be surprised when people become afraid of difference," she said.
The three-day conference, organised by the International Dialogue Centre (KAICIID) and the Allied Coordinating Council of Islamic NGOs (ACCIN), carries the theme "Shared Futures: Dialogue for Resilient and Inclusive Cities".
Following earlier editions in Bangkok in 2023 and Davao in 2024, the conference closes on Oct 28 with joint proposals that participants will take back to their cities.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Azalina: Malaysia studies models for proposed Law Reform Commission
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The government is studying suitable models for a proposed Malaysian Law Reform Commission that aligns with the country's legal and administrative framework, Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said said.
The Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Law and Institutional Reform) said the assessment includes practices adopted in England and Wales, Australia, New Zealand, Canada, and India.
"The commission's proposed core functions include reviewing outdated laws, identifying inconsistencies and legislative gaps, and simplifying legal language," she said when winding up the policy-stage debate on the Supply Bill 2027 (2027 Budget ) for her portfolio in the Dewan Rakyat today.
Azalina said the proposed commission will also conduct research and comparative studies, carry out public consultations, and independently recommend legal reforms, including assisting in drafting bills for government consideration.
She said the Legal Affairs Division (BHEUU) has been studying the proposal since August 2023, focusing on the commission's functions, structure, and implementation model.
Azalina said the study will be followed by consultations with ministries, government agencies, legal practitioners, academics, and civil society.
A steering committee, which she will chair, has also been proposed to coordinate the study, with participation from central agencies and relevant ministries.
"The finalised findings and recommendations will be submitted to the cabinet for consideration before further developments are reported to the Dewan Rakyat," she said.
She said establishing the commission is essential to ensuring legal reform remains a continuous process, independent of changes in government or political leadership.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim announced during the tabling of the 2027 Budget on Oct 9 that the government was studying a proposal to establish the commission to identify outdated laws and legislative gaps.
Meanwhile, Azalina cited the Parliamentary Services Act 2025 (Act 869), which came into force on Oct 1 to restore Parliament's administrative autonomy after nearly three decades, as evidence of the unity government's commitment to institutional reform. — BERNAMA

Title: 609 locations in Kelantan identified as flood-prone ahead of Northeast monsoon
Article:
PASIR MAS: A total of 609 locations across Kelantan have been identified as flood-prone ahead of the Northeast Monsoon, which is expected to begin tomorrow.
Kelantan Drainage and Irrigation Department director Datuk Dr Siti Fairus Zakaria said Pasir Mas recorded the highest number of potentially affected locations at 200, followed by Machang (75), Kuala Krai and Kota Baru (64 each), Pasir Puteh (49), Tumpat (47), Gua Musang (45), Tanah Merah (24), Bachok (22) and Jeli (19).
She said flooding was caused not only by the proximity of settlements to rivers but also by inadequate drainage systems that could not cope with prolonged rainfall.
"One of the main causes of flooding in Kelantan, particularly during the Northeast Monsoon, is prolonged heavy rain, which causes river levels to rise and overflow into low-lying areas and riverside settlements.
"High tides can also impede river water from flowing into the sea, causing water to back up and increasing the risk of flooding.
"The situation is worsened by drains and waterways clogged with rubbish and other obstructions," she said when met at a handover ceremony for General Operations Force posts here today.
Siti Fairus said development and changes in land use could also increase surface runoff, causing water to flow more rapidly into low-lying areas.
She said the federal government's Sungai Golok Integrated River Basin Development Project (PLSB), covering Phases 1, 2 and 3 for RM3.044 billion, was expected to improve drainage capacity and reduce flood risks in the rapidly developing areas of Pasir Mas and Tumpat.
Phase 1 is expected to reduce flood risks and protect 16,800 residents across 260 sq km, including agricultural land, against floods under a 50-year average recurrence interval (ARI) protection standard.
"The project will also help stabilise a 26km stretch of the Malaysia-Thailand border against erosion and maintain a minimum navigation channel depth of three metres to ensure safe and smooth navigation.
"Phase 2 is expected to reduce flood-risk areas by 25,000ha and protect 25,000 residents, while stabilising a 40km stretch of the international border.
"Phase 3 is expected to reduce flood-risk areas by 15,000ha and protect 16,000 residents," she said.
She said the RM22 million Sungai Golok estuary dredging project was completed on Sept 6.
The project was expected to improve water flow from the estuary into the sea. It involved constructing 28,000 cubic metres of rock embankment and dredging 153,000 cubic metres of material, she added.
She said improvements to the drainage system would help reduce flood risks and minimise damage to lives and property, while supporting the development of residential, industrial and commercial areas.
"Overall, the Sungai Golok estuary conservation project will improve the safety and efficiency of the estuary while supporting local fishing activities and tourism," she said.
The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has
forecast three to five episodes
of continuous heavy rain during the initial phase of the 2026/2027 Northeast Monsoon, from November to January.
MetMalaysia director-general Dr Mohd Hisham Mohd Anip said the conditions could cause flooding in low-lying areas and locations near rivers.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Perkeso to provide rehabilitation aids to 2 journalists injured in Ipoh crash
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Social Security Organisation (Perkeso) will provide rehabilitation aids to two female media practitioners injured in an accident in Menglembu, Ipoh, early yesterday morning to support their recovery.
In a statement today, Perkeso said the incident was classified as an employment injury as they were travelling for an official assignment and both were covered under the Employees' Social Security Act 1969 under the Lindung Pekerja scheme.
Malaysian National News Agency (Bernama) journalist Nur Afiradina Arshad, 34, sustained a neck injury requiring a neck brace, abrasions on her body, and a sprained ankle that had become swollen.
"She received treatment at Raja Permaisuri Bainun Hospital (HRPB) and was discharged on Sunday. She has been given one month of medical leave and Perkeso will provide her with suitable rehabilitation aids upon receiving the medical report from her doctor.
"Meanwhile, The New Straits Times journalist Zaharatulhayat Mat Arif, who sustained swelling to her cheek and both hands, received outpatient treatment at HRPB and was given three days of medical leave.
"We will continue to monitor her condition in the event she needs to extend her medical leave for a full recovery," it said.
According to the organisation, Nur Afiradina, who does not have Perkeso contributions, will have her case referred to the relevant agencies through the Social Synergy programme so that appropriate assistance can be considered based on her needs and eligibility.
In the 5.45am incident, the car carrying the journalists was travelling from
Ipoh to Bagan Datuk
to cover an official programme involving Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi.
The car had stopped at a traffic light junction near Taman Kledang Permai when it was hit from behind by a lorry.
Perkeso said the two victims did not need to visit its office as the Perkeso Prihatin Squad had obtained their information shortly after the incident to facilitate the processing of claims.
"This approach clearly reflects the transformation of Perkeso's current work culture, which proactively embraces the concept of seeking out contributors rather than merely observing and waiting.
"This change is to ensure that social security protection reaches those in need without delay. The world has changed and the way we work has to change accordingly. It is no longer the same as before," it said.
Perkeso also gave its assurance that it would continue to monitor the health of both journalists to ensure that appropriate assistance and support could be given.
"The safety and well-being of media practitioners, who often face high risks in the field, have always been a priority. Perkeso also wishes both journalists a speedy recovery," it said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Zahid explains RM2.1bil overspending on rural development projects
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The alleged RM2.1 billion in "overspending" on rural roads does not prove leakage or misappropriation, Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said.
Zahid, who is also rural and regional development minister, said the figure was derived by comparing actual expenditure of RM6.108 billion with the original allocation of RM3.982 billion, without taking into account the revised allocation.
"However, when compared with the revised allocation, actual expenditure remained below the amount available, leaving a balance of about RM34.3 million.
"Where did the RM2.1 billion figure come from? It was derived by subtracting the original allocation of RM3.982 billion from actual expenditure of RM6.108 billion, without taking into account the revised allocation.
"The RM2.1 billion difference against the original allocation is not proof of missing funds, leakage or misappropriation," he said during the winding-up debate on the 2027 Supply Bill in the Dewan Rakyat today.
He said the programme's financial position should be assessed by distinguishing between the original allocation, revised allocation and actual expenditure, rather than comparing spending with the original allocation alone.
He said additional allocations were made through an adjustment process to meet project payment requirements, including when work progressed faster than expected or outstanding claims for earlier projects had to be settled.
However, he said this did not allow ministries to spend money at their discretion, as every adjustment remained subject to government approval and established procedures.
"This means that a minister's instruction alone does not authorise the immediate spending of funds.
"Government financial approvals and procedures must still be followed," he said.
As of Sept 30, Zahid said the rural roads programme covered 415 projects at various stages of implementation, with a total cost of about RM34.23 billion.
He said expenditure for this year stood at about RM2.48 billion as of the same date, out of a revised allocation of RM3.02 billion, representing 82.1 per cent.
For 2027, he said the ministry had been allocated RM2.266 billion, with priority given to projects under construction, existing commitments and the settlement of outstanding payments.
"Our priority is to complete ongoing projects, settle legitimate payments and ensure that new commitments are aligned with the government's financial capacity," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: SKA Capital unit secures RM89.28mil contracts for TNB projects
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: SKA Capital Bhd's subsidiary, SKA Rekabina Sdn Bhd, has secured six contracts worth RM89.28 million from Ibrahim & Sons Sdn Bhd for Tenaga Nasional Bhd (TNB) projects.
The projects involve the installation of 11-kilovolt (kV) and 33kV underground cables and related accessories, as well as the construction of 33/11kV main distribution substations in Kuantan and Chendering.
They also include underground cable laying and jointing works for TNB's distribution network in Selangor.
In a filing with Bursa Malaysia, SKA Capital said the projects are expected to be completed within 18 months of commencement.
The contracts are expected to contribute positively to the group's revenue, earnings and net assets.

Title: Ramkarpal: Time to review death penalty for non-murder offences
Article:
PETALING JAYA: Malaysia should consider abolishing the death penalty for offences other than murder, following legal reforms introduced since 2023, says Bukit Gelugor MP Ramkarpal Singh.
The former deputy minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Law and Institutional Reform) said the proposal could secure bipartisan support in parliament, given developments following the abolition of mandatory death sentences three years ago.
He said all applications for review of death sentences in drug trafficking cases had been approved, with the sentences commuted to imprisonment.
"I believe there is bipartisan support for abolishing the death penalty for offences other than murder.
"I think now is the right time to explore this possibility, and I believe it can be done," he said.
Ramkarpal was speaking during a panel discussion titled The Pathway to Abolition of the Death Penalty in Malaysia at the "Ahead of Ending the Death Penalty in Asia: Reform Pathways, Comparative Perspectives, and Path Forward" conference here today.
He said abolishing the death penalty entirely would not require amendments to the Federal Constitution, as the relevant laws could be amended with a simple majority in parliament.
However, he said further discussions were needed on abolishing the death penalty for murder, as some groups remained strongly in favour of retaining it.
"For murder cases, there are still people who strongly support the death penalty, and I believe more engagement sessions should be held with these groups.
"For offences other than murder, I believe the proposal would receive bipartisan support in parliament," he said.
Meanwhile, Prime Minister's Department Legal Affairs Division (BHEUU) deputy director-general (Policy and Development) Datuk Dr Punitha Silivarajoo said the cabinet had agreed to establish a special committee to study a moratorium on the death penalty and the way forward for its full abolition.
She said the review would also examine the position of prisoners still awaiting execution and the offences that could be considered for abolition of the death penalty.
"The cabinet agreed that another special committee should be established to study the moratorium, the next steps and the way forward towards full abolition of the death penalty, if necessary.
"However, based on our experience in 2018, 2019 and 2023, comprehensive engagement must be held again, as we cannot simply decide to abolish the death penalty entirely," she said.
Earlier, Monash University Malaysia president and pro vice-chancellor Prof Datuk Dr Adeeba Kamarulzaman said Malaysia's success in abolishing mandatory death sentences showed that reforms once considered impossible could be achieved through evidence, advocacy and political will.
"Malaysia's adoption of a harm-reduction approach to tackling drug problems and its abolition of mandatory death sentences were once considered politically impossible.
"However, both were achieved through evidence, advocacy and political will, which opened the way for different approaches," she said.
The conference was organised by Monash University Malaysia, Rashid Zulkifli Advocates and Solicitors, the Office of the United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights (OHCHR) and the Anti-Death Penalty Asia Network (ADPAN).
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Madani govt resolves 12 MA63 matters, highest under any administration
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Madani government has resolved 12 matters under the Malaysia Agreement 1963 (MA63), the highest number settled by any administration.
Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Sabah and Sarawak Affairs) Datuk Mustapha Sakmud said the achievement reflected the government's efforts to address long-standing issues that had remained under negotiation for years.
"Of all the governments so far, the Madani government has resolved the highest number of matters that had been negotiated for a long time.
"Twelve matters have been resolved, while previous administrations settled only four. Why were these issues not given serious and thorough attention before?
"Fairness must be given, as these matters had long been neglected. Now that we have opened up avenues for discussion, it seems we are expected to resolve everything before the general election," he said during the winding-up session on the 2027 Supply Bill in the Dewan Rakyat.
The status of MA63 implementation came under scrutiny earlier, with several MPs pressing Mustapha for updates on outstanding matters.
They included Datuk Willie Mongin (GPS-Puncak Borneo), Datuk Seri Dr Jeffrey G Kitingan (GRS-Keningau), Datuk Ewon Benedick (GRS-Penampang) and Mohd Kurniawan Naim Moktar (BN-Kinabatangan).
Mustapha said decisions on MA63 matters required agreement between the federal government and the Sabah and Sarawak governments, adding that the process did not rest solely with the federal government.
On the proposal for Sabah and Sarawak to hold one-third of parliamentary seats, he suggested setting up a special committee under the technical committee to examine the matter.
However, he said the issue fell under the purview of Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Law and Institutional Reform) Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said.
"As a Sabahan myself, I want to see an increase in parliamentary seats for Sabah and Sarawak.
"We need to increase the number because the spirit of MA63 requires sufficient representation to ensure the voices of Sabah and Sarawak are heard in this House," he added.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysia to benefit from cross-border electricity project with Vietnam, Singapore
Article:
SINGAPORE: Malaysia stands to benefit from a cross-border electricity project involving Petroliam Nasional Bhd (Petronas) and Tenaga Nasional Bhd (TNB) through local contractor participation, engineering expertise and the development of renewable energy certificate mechanisms, said Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Fadillah Yusof.
Fadillah, who is also the energy transition and water transformation minister, said the project, involving the purchase of offshore wind energy from Vietnam and its transmission to Singapore, would create opportunities for Malaysian contractors to participate in the development of transmission infrastructure, including undersea cables.
"When you are doing the transmission line, definitely you need contractors and the contractors will be from Malaysia.
"In terms of human capital, this will be another learning curve for our engineers, and because it is the first time we are involved in a project with Vietnam, we will be learning about wind energy supply," he told Bernama on the sidelines of Singapore International Energy Week 2026 (SIEW 2026).
[[nid:1564000]]
Under the project, Petronas and TNB, through the MY Energy Consortium (MYEC), will work with PetroVietnam Technical Services Corporation (PTSC) to develop the cross-border electricity supply arrangement involving offshore wind energy from Vietnam.
Fadillah said Malaysia could also contribute its expertise in developing a mechanism for exchanging renewable energy certificates with Vietnam, which he said was crucial to the project's commercial viability.
"Vietnam has not developed that, so our experts can jointly develop with them how they can benefit in terms of renewable energy certificates.
"Otherwise the project will not be viable without the renewable energy certificate," he said.
The Energy Market Authority (EMA) of Singapore has granted conditional approval to Sembcorp Utilities Pte Ltd and its consortium partners to import 1.3 gigawatts (GW) of electricity into Singapore.
The approval allows the project to source and integrate low-carbon electricity from regional and domestic resources, including offshore wind energy from Vietnam and solar power from Malaysia.
Sembcorp Utilities is working towards commencing electricity imports under the project by 2035, subject to the necessary approvals, power purchase agreements and financing arrangements.
Fadillah said about 30 per cent of the electricity from the Vietnam offshore wind arrangement would be supplied to Peninsular Malaysia, with the majority transmitted to Singapore.
On broader regional energy cooperation, he said the initiative underscored the importance of developing the Asean Power Grid, which would enable member states to exchange electricity based on their respective energy resources and supply requirements.
"Why do we need the Asean Power Grid? It is not only for Malaysia. It is for the entire Asean. Every country has its own advantages," he said.
He cited Laos' hydropower and wind resources, as well as Thailand's solar and gas resources, as examples of how regional electricity connectivity could allow countries to complement one another's energy mix.
"When there is a shortage, we can exchange across border. We can buy from our neighbours.
"When we have surplus, we can also supply to them," he said.
He said the regional grid would help ensure security and stability of electricity supply while keeping costs affordable by allowing countries to share resources rather than invest individually in all the generation capacity they require.
"One is to make sure that there is a secure supply, number two is stability of supply, and number three is affordability," he said.
He said the Laos-Thailand-Malaysia-Singapore (LTMS) Power Integration Project was already an operational model for cross-border electricity trading, with efforts underway to extend similar arrangements to other Asean member states.
The existing arrangement connects Laos, Thailand, Malaysia and Singapore, while Vietnam had agreed to participate and further discussions were needed with Cambodia, he said.
Indonesia was already purchasing electricity from Sarawak through an interconnection with West Kalimantan, while the Philippines had also agreed in principle to connect to the regional grid through Sarawak, he added.
Fadillah said Asean members hoped to firm up the arrangements next year, moving beyond the existing memoranda of understanding (MoUs) towards a more concrete regional framework.

Title: Haze eases as Northeast Monsoon set to begin
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Hazy conditions across the country have improved following a change in wind direction.
The Malaysian Meteorological Department said the Northeast Monsoon, which begins tomorrow, would stop transboundary haze from drifting into Malaysia.
Its director-general, Dr Mohd Hisham Mohd Anip, said continuous northeasterly winds would keep transboundary haze away.
"The hazy weather has recovered since yesterday following a change in the direction of wind movement in our country, except in Sarawak.
"With the start of the Northeast Monsoon season tomorrow, the continuous movement of wind from the northeast will cause haze from neighbouring countries to no longer move towards our country," he told the New Straits Times.
Most areas nationwide recorded
good or moderate Air Pollutant Index
readings as of 7am today, as haze conditions continued to improve.
Malaysia has experienced haze since August due to forest and peatland fires in Indonesia, causing school closures, an increase in respiratory-related illnesses and flight disruptions.
Hisham said wet weather was expected in most areas this week.
"With the start of the Northeast Monsoon season, the weather throughout this week is expected to be wet in most areas, with rain expected in the early morning in the east coast states of the peninsula and rain with thunderstorms in the afternoon and evening in other areas," he said.
It said on Oct 23 that the 2026/2027
Northeast Monsoon
was expected to begin on Oct 27 and last until March 2027. Three to five episodes of continuous heavy rain were forecast between November and January, which could cause flooding in low-lying areas and near rivers.
Satellite observations on Oct 14 showed extensive clusters of hotspots in southern Sumatra and parts of Kalimantan, with monsoon winds carrying smoke into Peninsular Malaysia, western Sarawak and Singapore.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Son takes on BN stronghold after father's five election defeats
Article:
MELAKA: Losing five times in elections has not deterred his father from serving the community, and now Mohammad Mukhlisul Mubin Julasapiyah hopes to carry that fight forward by wresting the Kuala Linggi state seat from Barisan Nasional (BN).
The 25-year-old Pakatan Harapan (PH) candidate from Amanah acknowledged the challenge of contesting a seat that has long been an Umno stronghold but said political struggles required patience and sustained effort.
His father, Julasapiyah Kassim, first contested the Kuala Linggi seat in 1999. Although he has yet to win an election, his service and contributions to the local community remain remembered.
However, the Universiti Kebangsaan Malaysia law graduate said he did not regard his father's contributions as a ticket to securing votes, stressing that he had to earn and prove himself worthy of the electorate's trust.
"The people's trust is something I must earn and prove for myself," he said when contacted today.
Mukhlisul Mubin said losing an election did not necessarily mean a person had failed to serve the community, adding that efforts to help the people should not stop simply because a candidate failed to win.
"Losing an election does not mean we have failed to serve. Stopping our service just because we lost is the real failure," he said.
He said his candidacy also carried a message that young people should be given opportunities to take part in national leadership rather than being regarded merely as leaders of the future.
He said his involvement in politics began during his university days, where he gained exposure and experience that prepared him for a move into national politics.
"Young people today are leaders of the present. If we remain trapped in the mindset that young people are only leaders of the future, the political arena will remain closed to them indefinitely," he said.
The winner of the Education Malaysia Jordan International Speech Competition 2025 described the opportunity to contest an election as particularly meaningful, especially for young people seeking to bring fresh voices and ideas into politics.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: British policeman drives, collects and celebrates classic Protons
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: More than three decades after Proton cars first entered the United Kingdom market, the Malaysian marque continues to attract enthusiasts, including a British policeman who has built a personal collection of six models.
Jon Coupland, who lives in Boston, Lincolnshire, said he was drawn to the distinctive designs of older Proton models, which have become increasingly rare in the UK.
His interest began in 2019 when he stumbled upon an online advertisement for a used Proton Saga 1.5 and decided to buy it.
[[nid:1564027]]
"Without hesitation, I went straight to the dealership, bought the Proton Saga 1.5 and drove it home.
"I realised Proton models had their own charm, but were increasingly being forgotten in the UK.
"Since then, I have wanted to bring these cars together to help keep the Proton name alive," he said.
His first purchase was a 1990 Proton Saga 1.5 SE LE UK Special Edition, which cost £700 (about RM4,000). The car remains in good condition, with an odometer reading of 48,000km.
Coupland said his interest grew as he realised how difficult it was to find Proton cars in the UK, where the marque is now available mainly through the used-car market.
He is particularly fond of early models such as the Saga and Iswara, whose styling and finishing set them apart from other cars commonly seen on European roads.
[[nid:1564026]]
"Proton cars are unique because of their attractive angular designs and reliability. Their exterior styling also stands out from that of other saloons, which can be rather boring.
"They are also relatively affordable," he said.
One of his other prized possessions is a 1989 Proton Saga 1.5GL Black Knight Edition, which attracted attention after being named a favourite in the unusual and unpopular cars category at the Festival of the Unexceptional: A Concours de l'Ordinaire.
[[nid:1564025]]
For maintenance, Coupland relies heavily on his father, an experienced mechanic who is also well-versed in Proton models in the UK.
"Trim components, such as exterior and interior accessories, are much harder to find than mechanical parts. I usually salvage them from vehicles that have been scrapped," he said.
Coupland also hopes to visit Proton City in Tanjong Malim, Perak, as well as the carmaker's factory and museum at the Proton Centre of Excellence in Subang Jaya, Selangor.
He shares his passion for the national carmaker through social media and YouTube.
Beyond collecting, Coupland uses a white Proton Saga Iswara as his daily drive to work, while his other cars are reserved for special occasions and local automotive exhibitions.
[[nid:1564024]]
Proton entered the international market on Nov 23, 1987, when then National Automobile Enterprise chairman Tan Sri Jamil Jan and Proton Cars (UK) Ltd chairman David Alan Brown signed a distribution agreement for the Proton Saga in the United Kingdom, Ireland, the Isle of Man and the Channel Islands.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: DAP contests seven Melaka seats based on winning chances, says Loke
Article:
MELAKA: DAP's decision to contest only seven seats in the 16th Melaka election was based on an assessment of its winning chances, party secretary-general Anthony Loke said.
He said the decision took into account the party's performance in the 2021 state election, when DAP finished second in several seats it lost, but placed third in Bemban.
"We want to ensure that our strength, resources and focus are concentrated on seats we can win. That is why we are contesting only seven seats this time.
"It is a tactical and strategic decision by the party to ensure that our efforts and focus are directed towards the seats we can win, namely the seven we are contesting, including the four seats held by our incumbents," he said.
Loke, who is the transport minister, said this to reporters after officiating a special financial assistance presentation ceremony for taxi, rental car, and school bus drivers here today.
At the ceremony, 283 taxi and rental car drivers received RM1,000 assistance vouchers each.
In the 2021 Melaka election, DAP's Tey Kok Kiew, who contested Bemban under the Pakatan Harapan banner, lost to Perikatan Nasional candidate Dr Mohd Yadzil Yaakub by 328 votes in a five-cornered contest involving Barisan Nasional and two independents.
On PH's strategy for the election, Loke said the coalition will focus on the 21 seats announced by Prime Minister and PH chairman Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim on Saturday.
"We are working together under PH, comprising three parties - DAP, Parti Keadilan Rakyat (PKR) and Parti Amanah Negara (Amanah) - and we are focusing on the 21 seats we are contesting. We are not involved in the others," he said.
PH is fielding 21 candidates from its three component parties in the state election, compared with 28 candidates in 2021.
The Election Commission (EC) has set Oct 31 for nomination, Nov 10 for early voting, and Nov 14 for polling.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: High Court allows 12 Ampang Jaya residents to challenge local plan
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The High Court's decision to grant 12 Ampang Jaya residents leave to challenge the Ampang Jaya Municipal Council Local Plan 2035 (RT MPAJ 2035) through judicial review marks a significant step in their bid to protect community interests.
In a statement, residents' action group TOLAK RT2035 claimed the plan, gazetted on Feb 6, 2025, contained fundamental flaws, including land-use changes that had not been made public.
The group also alleged that objections raised during a public hearing in 2022 had not been incorporated into the plan.
It said the court granted leave for the judicial review application, filed in May last year, after finding that the challenge raised arguable questions of law and fact warranting a full hearing.
"We believe that the local plan currently permits high-intensity developments in environmentally sensitive hilltop and hillslope areas, as well as established disaster-risk zones.
"Unsustainable developments threaten terrain stability, increase the risk of severe landslides and flash floods, and destroy the remaining natural environment," the group said.
It identified Bukit Antarabangsa, Taman Hillview, Ukay Perdana, Taman Melawati, Kemensah and Taman Ukay Heights as high-risk areas facing pressure from proposed intensive and mega developments.
The group said failing to challenge the plan would undermine the public's statutory right to object to future projects under the Town and Country Planning Act 1976.
The substantive judicial review hearing has been fixed for Nov 25. — BERNAMA
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Australia's Ingenia hits 9-month high on AVID's US$1.5bil buyout bid
Article:
AUSTRALIA: Ingenia Communities Group received a takeover proposal from AVID Property Group for A$2.2 billion (US$1.54 billion), sending the Australian property developer's shares to their highest close in nine months.
Ingenia, which develops and operates communities offering rental and holiday accommodation, has already received three bids from Warburg Pincus, sending its shares up more than 35 per cent since the first offer in September. The stock jumped as much as 9.1 per cent on Monday before closing up 5.0 per cent at A$5.
AVID's bid to buy all Ingenia shares at A$5.4 is higher than Warburg Pincus' latest offer of A$5.25 apiece and at a 13.4 per cent premium to Friday's closing price.
The Ingenia board has decided to enter into a process deed with AVID and give it a period of "soft exclusivity" of up to six weeks, the company said, terminating Warburg Pincus' access to its data room. Last week, Ingenia set an October 23 deadline to sign a process deed with Warburg Pincus.
The AVID offer, which has backing from an unnamed global sovereign wealth fund and a global financial sponsor, hinges on Ingenia terminating a planned A$992.5-million acquisition of Peet, announced in late August.
"Ingenia is clearly an attractive set of assets that've been underpriced due to a mix of the Peet deal terms and the general despondent sentiment towards residential real estate amidst several RBA rate hikes and the Federal Budget changes earlier this year," said Cameron Curko, CIO at Pitcher Partners.
"The arrival of a superior bid in that context is not surprising particularly as it was a case of participate or lose out on the opportunity."
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Indonesia extends share buyback policy until June 2027 amid market volatility
Article:
JAKARTA: Indonesia's Financial Services Authority (OJK) has extended a policy allowing listed companies to buy back their own shares without shareholder approval until June 2027, amid efforts to strengthen market stability following a sharp stock market sell-off.
OJK's chief executive of Capital Markets, Financial Derivatives and Carbon Exchange Supervision Hasan Fawzi said the extension, from December 2026, responded to requests from listed companies seeking greater certainty over the timeframe, with some considering current share prices favourable for such transactions.
"We also emphasise that these buybacks must not disregard the minimum free-float requirement, as this does not contradict our efforts to increase the proportion of shares available for public trading," he told a press conference here on Monday.
The extension follows a sharp decline in Indonesia's benchmark Jakarta Composite Index (IHSG) on Oct 16, which triggered a temporary trading halt after global index provider MSCI announced a possible reclassification of the country's equity market.
Hasan said the index subsequently gained 4.9 per cent during the Oct 19-23 trading week, after touching a low of 4,907.37 points on Oct 19, before closing at 5,439.2 points last Friday.
Meanwhile, Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX) president director Jeffrey Hendrik said global index provider FTSE Russell had reaffirmed Indonesia's classification as a Secondary Emerging Market during an online meeting on Oct 23, following discussions on reforms covering transparency, liquidity and market surveillance.
"FTSE Russell confirmed that its Oct 6 report clearly maintained Indonesia's classification as a Secondary Emerging Market. Indonesia was not even placed on its watchlist," he told the same press conference.
Jeffrey said IDX would introduce more targeted surveillance measures to detect suspected share price manipulation, including publicly announcing investigations and potentially restricting or suspending specific securities accounts, with consultations involving exchange members scheduled for this week.
He said IDX would also expand its High Shareholding Concentration committee to nine members, comprising four representatives from market self-regulatory organisations and five independent external members from the financial industry, academia and investment community.
He said the move was aimed at strengthening transparency, governance and the credibility of the process used to identify stocks with highly concentrated ownership.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Driver fined after viral video shows two men sitting on moving car roof
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Police have issued summonses to a driver after a viral video showed two men sitting on the roof of his moving car in Taman Puteri Wangsa, Ulu Tiram.
Johor Baru Selatan district police chief Assistant Commissioner Azrul Hisham Mohd Shaffei said police detected the video and photographs about 9am on Oct 24 after they were shared on the Info Bencana Pahang Facebook page.
"The driver, who was traced on Oct 25, was found to have been driving without insurance coverage or a valid driving licence," he said in a statement.
He said the
footage
showed the two men sitting on the roof of a blue Proton Wira as it travelled from Jalan Beladau 32 towards Jalan Bukit Jaya.
The summonses were issued under Sections 47, 26 and 23 of the Road Transport Act 1987 for carrying passengers in a dangerous manner, driving without insurance coverage and driving without a valid licence, respectively.
Police advised the public to comply with road laws and prioritise safety when using the roads.
The video, believed to have been recorded by a motorist travelling behind the car, showed a third person driving while the two men sat on the roof.
Despite the obvious risk of falling, they appeared carefree as the vehicle continued moving.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: KPKT moves to standardise short-term rental accommodation rules nationwide
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Ministry of Housing and Local Government (KPKT), through PLANMalaysia and in collaboration with the Ministry of Tourism, Arts and Culture (MOTAC), state governments and local authorities, is drafting STRA planning guidelines to serve as a uniform source of authority.
The move comes as the government seeks to require that only premises registered and fully compliant with local authority licensing conditions may legally operate short-term rental accommodation (STRA) nationwide, said Deputy Housing and Local Government Minister Datuk Aiman Athirah Sabu.
"Under this framework, strata premises remain bound by the provisions and by-laws of their respective Joint Management Bodies (JMB) or Management Corporations (MC) under the Strata Management Act 2013.
"To ensure full compliance, the government is also encouraging strategic cooperation with digital platform companies to implement an automatic licence status verification mechanism before any premises is listed," she said during the question-and-answer session in the Dewan Rakyat today.
She was responding to a question from Syerleena Abdul Rashid (PH-Bukit Bendera) on provisions requiring short-term accommodation platforms to verify licence status, delist unlicensed premises and regulate such operations.
Aiman Athirah said digital platform providers must take responsibility for delisting premises that are unlicensed or in breach of local authority conditions and existing laws, while enforcement agencies hold the legal power to act firmly against recalcitrant operators.
"Local authorities and enforcement agencies have the right to take legal action under the Town and Country Planning Act 1976 and the Street, Drainage and Building Act 1974, as well as by-laws, against stubborn operators and to ensure listings of illegal accommodation on service provider portals are blocked," she said.
On the guidelines, she said the document is now in the final review stage with MOTAC before being raised for the Cabinet's consideration.
"The document will be tabled at the National Council for Local Government (MNKT) for mutual agreement before being adopted by state and local authorities nationwide," she said.
Aiman Athirah praised the Penang state government for moving ahead in regulating the sector through the gazetting of local by-laws.
"Penang has implemented the Guidelines for the Operation of Private Accommodation in Strata Property Schemes from April 1, 2023 and has enforced the Private Accommodation (Local Authority) By-Laws from Aug 1, 2026," she said.
On the proposal to cap rentals at 180 nights, Aiman Athirah said a regulatory impact assessment had already been carried out during the preparation of the initial regulatory framework.
"Any cap must take into account the opportunity for premises to generate income while meeting the needs of the tourism industry, and must also prioritise public safety and order as well as the wellbeing of residents," she said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Melaka polls: DAP skips Bemban due to slim chances of winning, says Loke
Article:
MELAKA: DAP has decided not to contest the Bemban seat in the Melaka election after assessing that its chances of winning were slim.
DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke Siew Fook said the decision was made on strategic grounds to ensure the party could focus its machinery, resources and attention on seven seats where it stood a better chance of winning.
He said DAP assessed each seat based on its chances of winning rather than simply considering the party's traditional position in a particular constituency.
He said Bemban was the only seat contested by DAP in the previous election where the party finished third, while it came second in the other seats it failed to win.
"Firstly, this is a strategic decision by the party. We assess every seat we contest based on our ability to win.
"Based on our results in the previous election, Bemban was the only seat we contested where we finished third, rather than second," he said.
He was speaking at a press conference after the Special Financial Assistance Presentation Ceremony for taxi, rental car and school bus drivers at the CMI Complex Auditorium here today.
Loke said DAP did not want to spread its strength and resources across too many constituencies at the expense of the seats it was contesting.
"We want to ensure our strength and resources, including our focus, are concentrated on seats we can win.
"That is why we are contesting only seven seats this time, excluding Bemban. This is a technical and strategic decision made by the party," he said.
He said four of the seven seats contested by DAP in the election were seats it currently held, making defending them one of the party's priorities.
On dissatisfaction over seat allocation, Loke said this was not unusual within a political party.
He said decisions on seat allocation and candidate selection were made by the top leadership after considering various factors, although some might hold differing views.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysia's private hospitals enter a new expansion cycle amid rising demand
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's private hospital operators are embarking on a new expansion cycle, driven by existing hospital expansions, acquisitions and new developments, as healthcare groups seek to capture growing demand.
Maybank Investment Bank (Maybank IB) said new private hospital investments remained concentrated in established healthcare markets, namely the Klang Valley, Penang, Johor and Melaka.
"These markets warrant closer attention given differences in local demographics, specialist availability, medical tourism exposure and existing competition," it said.
Among the key players, KPJ Healthcare Bhd aims to increase its capacity to about 6,000 beds by 2030, while IHH Healthcare Bhd targets more than 4,000 beds across its Malaysian operations by the same year.
Sunway Medical Centre (SunMed) expects to expand its capacity to more than 3,400 beds by 2032.
Meanwhile, PMCK Bhd plans to add a 90-bed hospital in Kulim, with operations targeted to begin in the first quarter of 2028.
Thomson Medical Group is also expanding its footprint. Its Thomson Hospital Kota Damansara currently has 399 operational beds, against a total capacity of 554 beds, while its proposed 500-bed Thomson Hospital Iskandariah in Johor Baru is targeted for completion in 2030.
"We believe the rate of occupancy growth in new hospitals is largely dependent on local demand conditions and competition from existing private hospitals within the area.
It cited KPJ Kuala Selangor as an example of successful market entry, noting that the hospital achieved positive earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation (EBITDA) in less than a year by serving an underserved market.
The nearest multispecialty private hospital competitor, Columbia Asia Klang, is about 50km away. Early marketing efforts and adoption by insurer panels also supported the hospital's performance.
Similarly, SunMed's proposed 325-bed hospital in Putrajaya, targeted to begin operations in 2031, offers an opportunity to serve a relatively underserved market.
Located next to Putrajaya Terminal and Destina Putrajaya, the hospital would be accessible from Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) in about 30 minutes by road via the ELITE highway, or 22 minutes via the KLIA Transit rail service. It would also be about 40 minutes from Sultan Abdul Aziz Shah Airport in Subang.
Maybank IB said the proposed hospital faced limited private-sector competition, with the existing Stella Kasih Medical Centre offering 32 beds about 10 minutes away by car. The adjacent Putrajaya Public Hospital had an occupancy rate of 61 per cent at the time of the report.
The investment bank said the project could tap into an affluent patient base, with Putrajaya's average household income at RM14,000 a month, compared with the national mean of RM9,000.
It added that the hospital would also be accessible to the southern Klang Valley and could offer an attractive proposition for medical tourism as one of the tertiary healthcare facilities closest to KLIA. Columbia Asia Puchong is about 44km from the airport.
Maybank IB maintained a "neutral" view on SunMed's proposed Putrajaya hospital in the near term, as the project had already been incorporated into its discounted cash flow-based sum-of-the-parts target price of RM2.01 for SunMed.
However, higher revenue intensity, faster breakeven and stronger foreign-patient volumes could provide upside to its earnings estimates.
Its sensitivity analysis showed that every RM1,000 increase in its estimated average revenue per inpatient for the proposed hospital would raise its target price by 2.0 per cent.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: TNB, Petronas-backed regional power project secures Singapore's conditional approval
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Tenaga Nasional Bhd (TNB) and Petroliam Nasional Bhd (Petronas) are moving closer to developing a regional renewable electricity corridor linking Vietnam, Malaysia and Singapore, following conditional approval from Singapore's Energy Market Authority.
The approval was granted to Sembcorp Utilities Pte Ltd, a subsidiary of Singapore-listed Sembcorp Industries, for a project that aims to supply Singapore with up to 1.3 gigawatts of renewable electricity through the Vietnam-Malaysia-Singapore initiative.
The project will combine offshore wind power from Vietnam with solar energy and battery storage facilities in Malaysia, with electricity imports expected to begin in 2035.
Under the proposed arrangement, electricity generated in Vietnam would be transmitted through Malaysia, which would serve as both a recipient of renewable power and a transit point for supplies destined for Singapore.
The approval follows a joint development agreement signed in May 2025 between three parties: PetroVietnam Technical Services Corp, a member of Vietnam National Industry–Energy Group; Sembcorp Utilities, the project's designated electricity importer; and MY Energy Consortium, comprising TNB and Petronas.
"The approval provides a basis for the participating consortia to advance the next stages of project development, subject to the necessary regulatory and project approvals," the parties said in a joint statement.
The conditional approval was formally presented at the opening of Singapore International Energy Week 2026 on Oct 26.
Since signing the agreement, the participating consortia have undertaken technical and commercial work with governments, regulators and other stakeholders across the three countries.
The approval reflects the progress made in developing the project and cooperation among the participating parties, according to the statement.
The initiative also aims to tap Southeast Asia's renewable energy potential, strengthen cross-border electricity connectivity and support the development of the Asean Power Grid.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Pahang exports hit RM10.95bil in first eight months, signalling growth potential
Article:
KUANTAN: Pahang recorded RM10.95 billion in exports in the first eight months of this year, highlighting the state's potential for further growth.
Malaysia External Trade Development Corporation (Matrade) chief executive officer Datuk Abu Bakar Yusof said the state remained resilient, supported by strong economic fundamentals and promising growth prospects.
"Exports of machinery and transport equipment surged 412.8 per cent in the first eight months of this year compared with the same period last year, while fuels and lubricants grew 47.9 per cent and food products increased 15.8 per cent.
"These figures present opportunities to diversify Pahang's export base and enable more local entrepreneurs to participate in international trade," he said at the 2026 Pahang Export Day.
The second edition of the event was opened by Pahang Investment, Industry, Science, Technology and Innovation Committee chairman Datuk Mohd Nizar Najib.
Abu Bakar said Kuantan remained a key driver of Pahang's economy, supported by its services, trade, logistics and petrochemical sectors.
"Each district has its own strengths, with Bentong contributing through tourism and agrofood, while Temerloh continues to grow through trade and aquaculture.
"Cameron Highlands is known for its highland agriculture, Raub for premium durian production and Pekan for its automotive industry. Plantation, fisheries and ecotourism activities also contribute to the state's economic diversity," he said.
He said Pahang could translate these district-level strengths into broader export opportunities by adding value to locally produced goods, enhancing the competitiveness of micro, small and medium enterprises, and connecting local products with international buyers.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Arroyo: Malaysia's reforms could pave way for death penalty abolition
Article:
PETALING JAYA: Ex-Philippine president Gloria Arroyo said Malaysia's move to abolish the mandatory death penalty could pave the way for full abolition.
The Abolition of Mandatory Death Penalty Act 2023 was passed by parliament in April 2023 and came into force on July 4 that year, giving judges discretion to impose the death penalty or an alternative prison term for offences previously subject to mandatory capital punishment.
Arroyo said gradual reforms were important to achieving full abolition and ensuring the changes could be sustained.
Replacing death sentences with other penalties, imposing a moratorium on executions and abolishing the mandatory death penalty could lay the groundwork for wider reform, she said.
"First, the sequence of reforms matters. Replacing death sentences with other penalties, a moratorium and the abolition of the mandatory death penalty, as Malaysia has so courageously done, can change the landscape and pave the way for the full abolition of the death penalty," she said.
Arroyo, a commissioner of the International Commission Against the Death Penalty, said the Philippines' experience showed that abolition required strong evidence, political leadership and broad support.
The Philippines abolished the death penalty under its 1987 Constitution, reinstated it in 1993 and abolished it again in 2006, during Arroyo's presidency from 2001 to 2010.
Evidence of judicial errors was among the main factors behind abolition. In the 2004 case of People v. Mateo, the Philippine Supreme Court reported that only 230 of 907 death sentences reviewed since 1993 were upheld, while 651 were modified or overturned, including 65 acquittals.
"When a system makes mistakes that frequently, while an execution cannot be undone, the argument for the death penalty becomes untenable," she said.
A 2004 study by the Free Legal Assistance Group of 1,121 death row inmates found that 73 per cent were poor, while less than one per cent came from the upper class.
In April 2006, Arroyo commuted the death sentences of more than 1,000 prisoners to life imprisonment. The move was followed by cross-party cooperation in Congress, leading to the signing of Republic Act No. 9346, which prohibits the death penalty, on June 24, 2006.
The Philippines joined the Second Optional Protocol to the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights in 2007 to strengthen safeguards against reinstatement.
Arroyo warned that abolition was not necessarily permanent, as public fear of crime and political pressure could lead to the death penalty being reintroduced. Efforts to reinstate it in the Philippines continued, particularly for drug offences. A bill passed by the House of Representatives in 2017 was not pursued in the Senate.
She said abolition should be accompanied by a justice system trusted by the public, including effective police enforcement, fair courts and support for crime victims.
"The death penalty does not make our societies safer, but makes them less just," she said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: British nationals top KLIA drug mule arrests, drugs worth RM202.76m seized
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 26 — A total of 77 cases linked to drug mule syndicates at Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) were recorded between January and Oct 15, with 93 individuals arrested.
Bukit Aman Narcotics Crime Investigation Department (NCID) director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said these cases involved the seizure of 2,526.28 kilogrammes (kg) of drugs, with an estimated value of RM202.76 million.
He said the seized substances comprised 2,407.27 kg of cannabis (64 cases), 77.837 kg of methamphetamine (four cases), 22.11 kg of ketamine (four cases), 15.585 kg of cocaine (three cases), and 3.475 kg of a mixture of ketamine and cannabis (two cases).
“Out of the total 93 arrests, nationals from the United Kingdom accounted for the highest number at 26, followed by Malaysia (23), Singapore (11), Japan (five), and France (six).
“Meanwhile, there were two individuals each from Hong Kong, Indonesia, India, Ireland, Portugal, and Germany and one individual each from the Netherlands, Greece, Sweden, Slovakia, the United States, Brazil, Uganda, Zambia, Thailand, and China,” he said when contacted by Bernama today.
Regarding the breakdown of the 77 cases, he said 45 cases were recorded through the cooperation of enforcement agencies comprising 41 cases handled by Aviation Security (AVSEC) Auxiliary Police of Malaysia Airports Holdings Bhd (MAHB) at KLIA, and four cases by the Malaysia Border Control and Protection Agency (AKPS).
“Another 25 cases involved actions by the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) and the Narcotics Crime Investigation Department (NCID), including the KLIA Narcotics Crime Investigation Division and the Selangor contingent police headquarters (IPK).
“Additionally, seven cases were recorded through follow-up operations, which led to the arrest of 12 individuals and the seizure of 571.59 kilogrammes of cannabis flowers,” he said.
Hussein noted that these successes reflect the ongoing commitment of the department, in collaboration with relevant enforcement agencies, to combat drug smuggling and curb syndicates that exploit individuals as drug mules.
“The public is also reminded not to be easily deceived by suspicious job offers or promises of lucrative rewards especially those involving the transport of luggage or items belonging to others to foreign countries.
“Furthermore, the public is urged to refrain from carrying items belonging to other people abroad without knowing their contents, and to report any suspicious activities to the police,” he said. — Bernama

Title: MACC seeks 24-year-old man to assist Sabah corruption probe, last traced to Semporna
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 26 — The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) is seeking a local man to assist in an investigation in Sabah.
In a statement today, MACC identified the man as Jamaluddin Jamahali, 24, who is being investigated under Section 17(b) of the MACC Act 2009.
The commission said attempts to contact him and locate him at his last known address in Kampung Keramat, Semporna, Sabah, had been unsuccessful.
Anyone who knows his whereabouts or has relevant information is urged to contact investigating officer Abu Hudzaifah Abd Talib at 014-8573727 or via email at hudzaifah@sprm.gov.my. — Bernama

Title: Zahid rejects RM2.1b overspending claims, says ministry underspent revised allocation
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 26 — Rural and Regional Development Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi today dismissed claims that his ministry overspent by RM2.1 billion, saying the figure reflected the difference between its original allocation and revised spending ceiling over three years.
Winding up the 2027 Budget debate in the Dewan Rakyat, Zahid said the ministry spent RM6.108 billion between 2023 and 2025, against a revised allocation of RM6.143 billion after additional funding was approved,
Free Malaysia Today
reported.
“When we compare the amended allocations, the ministry has in fact underspent,” he was quoted as saying.
The explanation follows calls by DAP Bagan MP Lim Guan Eng last month for the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission to investigate what he described as excess spending by the ministry.
The issue drew attention after Zahid voiced concern over delays in payments to contractors involved in ministry projects, saying some had been forced to cease operations because of cash flow problems despite completing their work.
Treasury secretary-general Johan Mahmood Merican later attributed the delays to the ministry's spending commitments, noting that most of this year's allocation for rural road projects had already been utilised.
According to Johan, spending on rural road projects reached RM1.8 billion in 2023 against an approved allocation of RM1.1 billion, RM2 billion in 2024 compared with RM1.3 billion allocated, and RM2.3 billion in 2025 against RM1.6 billion approved.

Title: Langkawi’s duty-free overhaul: RM300,000 vehicle price cap and RM10,000 spending limit
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 26 — The duty-free status of Langkawi is not intended to allow wealthy individuals to keep luxury vehicles on the island for several years before bringing them into the Principal Customs Area to avoid paying higher taxes.
Deputy Finance Minister Liew Chin Tong said changes to the duty and tax exemption policy for vehicles were introduced not only to address revenue leakage but also to discourage such business practices.
“At its core, this is a business model that we do not wish to promote, and we hope this policy will be accepted by all citizens,” he said in reply to a supplementary question from Datuk Mohd Suhaimi Abdullah (PN-Langkawi) during the Special Chamber session in the Dewan Rakyat today.
Mohd Suhaimi had sought clarification on the government’s review of the RM300,000 threshold for vehicle tax exemptions in Langkawi and called for stricter enforcement to prevent abuse of the facilities.
Liew acknowledged that some business operators would be affected by the policy but stressed that local residents would not be impacted.
Earlier, he said that, effective Jan 1, 2026, duty and tax exemptions for vehicles would be capped at a value of RM300,000 to prevent wealthy individuals from abusing the incentives to acquire luxury vehicles.
He said the threshold was reasonable and sufficient to meet the needs of local residents, car rental operators, taxi services and commercial vehicle users, while ensuring that the exemptions remained focused on vehicles used for daily activities and local business operations.
“Although there have been changes to the tax exemption policy for certain products on Langkawi Island, its status as a Duty-Free Island remains in effect,” he added.
Meanwhile, Liew said the government had announced in Budget 2027 an increase in the eligibility threshold for duty-free purchases by visitors and tourists from RM1,000 to RM10,000.
He said the revised threshold covered several additional categories of goods, including fashion accessories such as watches and handbags, electrical and electronic items, and textiles, while excluding tobacco products and motor vehicles.
